Internet & networking · 6/6

304 or 200 after a revalidation

304 Not Modified

  • Only headers cross the network
  • The cache reuses the stored body

200 OK

  • A new body crosses the network
  • The new response replaces the copy

Validation is a cheap question: has it changed?

A cache keeps a copy of a response.

Watch one browser cache reuse app.css.

The first request finds no stored copy.

The cache forwards it to the origin and

stores the 200 response with its headers.

A stored copy is fresh while its

lifetime is greater than its age.

Here max-age gives a lifetime of sixty seconds.

At thirty seconds the age is thirty, so the copy is fresh.

The cache answers alone, with no trip to the origin.

At ninety seconds the copy is stale.

The cache asks the origin with If-None-Match.

A 304 answer means keep your copy.

A 304 sends only headers, so the cache reuses the stored body.

A 200 sends a new body that replaces the copy.
